prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Sign in to safely back up your desktop pet and sync your companion across all your devices.", "Your pet choices and progress will be automatically saved to your account."]
1: ["Choose Your Desktop Pet Journey", "Select how you would like to bring your desktop pet to life today."]
2: ["Upload well-lit, clear front-facing photos to ensure your custom pet generates accurately."]
3: []
4: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion!", "Your pet is now active on your desktop. Right-click your pet anytime to access controls, talk, or hide it."]
5: []
6: ["Stuck on this screen? Check your internet connection or retry signing in."]
7: ["Discover Your Desktop Pet", "Prepare to adopt a virtual companion that lives and plays directly on your workspace.", "Get Started"]
8: ["Official Pet Adoption Certificate", "Give your new desktop companion a name to complete the adoption process."]
9: ["Look for your pet's system tray or menu bar icon if the companion doesn't appear on screen immediately."]
